positions.name: AeroVironment, Inc.
positions.sector: Electronic Technology — Aerospace & Defense (autonomous systems, loitering munitions, counter-UAS, directed energy)
positions.catalyst: AeroVironment reported fiscal Q1 FY2027 after the close on 9/9: adjusted EPS $0.59 vs. $0.30 consensus (a 97% beat) on revenue of $480.5M vs. ~$456-460M consensus, both records. The number that matters more than the beat is the backlog: funded backlog hit a record $1.5B, +37% y/y and +23% SEQUENTIALLY, on Q1 bookings of $0.7B and a book-to-bill of 1.4x, with trailing-twelve-month bookings above $3B. FY27 guidance was REAFFIRMED (not raised) at $2.125-2.225B revenue, $305-325M adj. EBITDA, $3.02-3.34 non-GAAP EPS. The quarter also carried the first production award in the directed-energy program of record — the $464.8M U.S. Army Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) contract for dozens of LOCUST X3 systems, announced 9/2, the first-ever production contract for a directed energy weapon in U.S. history. Stock closed 9/9 down 5.36% at $140.80 on 5.0M shares (2.8x its 1.79M average) into the print, then recovered to $144.22 after hours and is bid $150.00 / offered $150.30 pre-market this morning.
positions.driver: This is the setup the book has been losing money by NOT taking. The last several picks — CHYM yesterday, MU on 8/28 — were momentum names bought at or near 52-week highs after a +10% gap, into thin air, with no support beneath the entry. Every one of them round-tripped. AVAV is the structural opposite. ENTRY IS NOT A CHASE. $150.28 is +6.7% over yesterday's close, inside the 8-10% ceiling — but the more useful comparison is the 9/8 close of ~$148.77, against which this entry is only +1.0%. Yesterday's 5.4% drop was market-wide (Dow flush, oil shock), not company-specific, and the earnings beat has simply undone it. We are paying essentially the pre-flush price for a company that has since printed a record quarter. WHERE THE DOWNSIDE PROTECTION ACTUALLY COMES FROM: AVAV trades at $150 against a 52-week high of $417.86 (10/9/25) — it is 64% off its high and only 11% above its 52-week low of $135.20 set in June. Price-to-book is 1.71x on a $7.15B market cap. There is no crowded momentum long to unwind here; the de-rating already happened over eleven months. That is a fundamentally different risk profile from buying a name at a 52-week high, and it is why this one wins the 'most downside protection' half of the mandate rather than just the 'highest reward' half. THE STOP IS TECHNICAL, NOT ARBITRARY. $139.76 sits one cent below yesterday's session low of $139.77. To hit it, AVAV must not merely fade the earnings gap but trade through the entire prior session's range on a day it beat by 97%. That is a genuine invalidation, not noise. MACRO ALIGNMENT IS THE TIEBREAKER, and it is the same test that picked CHYM yesterday, applied to a better answer. The tape's two drivers are (1) an active U.S.-Iran shooting conflict — the U.S. struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two Navy warships, WTI is up six straight sessions and Brent is ~$99 — and (2) a Fed that fed funds futures now put at 59% odds of a 25bp HIKE on 9/15-16. AVAV's product line is the literal answer to driver (1): counter-UAS, loitering munitions, and ship-defense high-energy lasers are what you buy when drones and ballistic missiles are hitting your warships. It is not a proxy or a read-through; it is the order book. And on driver (2), AVAV at 1.7x book is far less exposed to multiple compression than the high-multiple growth names that got hit yesterday — the Fed-hike risk that made every other candidate on the board dangerous is smallest here. RUNNERS-UP AND WHY THEY LOST: ODD (+24% on a beat-and-raise) and JILL (+15%) had already made their entire move and are flat-to-down pre-market this morning — the catalyst is spent, there is nothing left to capture in 24h. SIG raised annual guidance but is quoted $102.66 against a $102.48 close, i.e. unchanged, with a $91.45 bid showing no real pre-market liquidity. GME double-beat and the market shrugged (+0.6%). AEO beat by $0.57 and is down 11.8% pre-market — proof that in this tape a beat alone buys nothing. Energy would be the direct war bet but crude is up six consecutive days and is the definition of chasing. AVAV is the only name on the board with a fresh, unspent, hard catalyst that has not yet been paid for.
positions.risks: (1) GUIDANCE WAS REAFFIRMED, NOT RAISED. This is the single biggest weakness in the thesis and it should not be glossed. A double beat with an unchanged full-year outlook implicitly guides the remaining three quarters slightly lower, and this is precisely the pattern that got AEO (-11.8%), BRZE (-11%), NAVN (-11%), KFY and SKIL punished this week. The market is in 'show me the forward number' mode, and AVAV did not give it one. The counter is the backlog — +23% sequentially and a 1.4x book-to-bill are forward numbers, just expressed as orders rather than as a guidance range — but a reaffirm is objectively weaker than a raise. (2) GAP-AND-FADE IS THE PRIMARY LOSS PATH AND THIS BOOK HAS LIVED IT REPEATEDLY. CHYM, MU, QCOM, IONQ and SEI all round-tripped their catalysts within a session. The marginal buyer has been absent all week. The mitigation here is structural rather than hopeful: the entry is only ~1% above the pre-flush price and the stock is 64% off its high, so there is far less air beneath it than in those trades — but the pattern is live and the stop exists for this reason. (3) AUGUST PPI PRINTS AT 8:30AM ET TODAY, INSIDE THE HOLD. This is unavoidable and is flagged deliberately: the entry is a pre-market limit placed BEFORE the PPI release, and the position carries through it into the open. With Brent near $99 after six straight up sessions, a hot energy-driven PPI is a live possibility and would push hike odds above 59%, hitting equities broadly. AVAV's low multiple limits the damage relative to a growth name, but it does not make it immune. (4) AUGUST CPI IS FRIDAY 9/11 AT 8:30AM ET — checked, and the rotation window closes ahead of it. The Friday 6:35am CT run exits at 7:35am ET, 55 minutes before the print, so this trade does NOT carry CPI risk. It does carry tonight's overnight Middle East headline risk in both directions. (5) NEGATIVE TRAILING EARNINGS. The trailing P/E is -25.9; GAAP EPS is negative, largely on BlueHalo acquisition amortization and integration costs. There is no earnings-based valuation floor, only the 1.7x book. A company with negative GAAP earnings can de-rate further on book value if integration disappoints. (6) DEFENSE IS HEADLINE-DRIVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The same escalation that supports the thesis reverses instantly on a de-escalation headline — a ceasefire, a negotiation, an Iranian climbdown. A 24-hour hold in a live geopolitical conflict is a two-sided bet, and this position is long the escalation side of it. (7) LIQUIDITY IS ADEQUATE BUT NOT DEEP. 1.79M shares average daily volume on a 38.1M float; the name has moved 5%+ on ordinary sessions and traded a 7.3% intraday range yesterday ($139.77-$150.05). Position size is trivial against that, but the volatility means the 7% stop is closer to a normal day's range than it looks.
